# WeatherClient

<!-- Generated by crucible. Change the model or the SDK configuration and regenerate. -->

The Swift client for the Weather API (`example.weather#Weather`, API version `2026-10-01`, sent as `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request), generated by [Crucible](https://github.com/Operation-Leyline/crucible) from the service's model.

## Install

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/OWNER/WeatherClient.git", from: "0.0.0-dev"), // the repository the package is published to
.product(name: "WeatherClient", package: "WeatherClient"), // in the dependencies of the target that calls the API
```

The package is `WeatherClient`, version `0.0.0-dev`; code refers to it as `WeatherClient`.

## Create a client

```swift
import Foundation
import WeatherClient

let client = try WeatherClient(ClientConfig(token: { ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["WEATHER_TOKEN"] }))
```

`token` is the bearer token source: an `async throws` closure returning the token, or `nil` to send none, called on every attempt so a refreshed token is used. The initializer throws for an invalid configuration; share one client, and call `close()` when finished. The client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request.

## Call an operation

`getCity` calls `GetCity`. Every operation has a method like it.

```swift
import Foundation
import WeatherClient

// The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
let client = try WeatherClient(ClientConfig(token: { ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["WEATHER_TOKEN"] }))

// Values from the model's example "Read a city".
let input = try GetCityInput(
    cityId: "c-0a1b2c3d",
    at: Timestamp(seconds: 1767323045 /* 2026-01-02T03:04:05Z */)
)

do {
    let output = try await client.getCity(input)
    print("city:", output.city)
    if let forecast = output.forecast { print("forecast:", forecast) }
    if let requestId = output.requestId { print("requestId:", requestId) }
} catch let error as NotFoundError {
    print("NotFoundError (HTTP \(error.metadata.status)):", error.message)
}
client.close()
```

## Pagination

A paginated operation also has a `<operation>Pages` method returning `Pages<Output>`, an `AsyncSequence` of pages (`for try await page in try client.listThingsPages(input)`): each page is one response, each step makes one call, and it stops when the response carries no next token.

```swift
import Foundation
import WeatherClient

// The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
let client = try WeatherClient(ClientConfig(token: { ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["WEATHER_TOKEN"] }))

// Values from the model's example "List the first page".
let input = ListCitiesInput(
    maxResults: 2,
    tags: [
        "coastal",
        "capital",
    ]
)

// Each page is one response; the paginator sends `nextToken` for the next.
for try await page in try client.listCitiesPages(input) {
    print(page.cities)
}
client.close()
```

## Errors

Each modelled error is a struct conforming to `WeatherException` and `ServiceError`: catch it with `catch let error as TheError` and read its properties and `metadata.status`. An error the client does not model is `UnknownServiceError`; a failure without a response throws `NetworkError`, and a call outlasting `ClientConfig.timeout` throws `TimeoutError`.

## Retries and idempotency

Calls are retried with backoff when a retry is safe: a modelled throttling error is retried for any operation; transport failures, HTTP 500, 502, 503 and 504 and other retryable modelled errors only for operations that are read-only, idempotent or carry an idempotency token. An idempotency token the caller leaves unset is generated once per call and reused on every attempt; set it yourself to replay one logical request across calls. These operations fill a token: `createCity` (`clientToken`). Set `maxAttempts` in `ClientConfig` to change the attempt limit (3, the first included; 1 turns retries off), and `baseDelay` and `maxDelay` for the backoff.
